pedagogy.problem_statement: A fire in one fifth-floor server room of one government building took down hundreds of public systems at once, and destroyed a shared drive that had no copy anywhere else.
pedagogy.core_thesis: On 26 September 2025 a lithium-ion battery fire at the NIRS data center in Daejeon knocked out 647 systems; most were restored from backups, but G-Drive, 858 TB of civil servants' files, had no external backup and was lost.
pedagogy.mental_model: A wall of labelled paper folders, one per public service, with copies on a distant shelf for all but one big folder in the middle; the fire scorches across the wall and only the folders with a shelf copy come back.
pedagogy.key_takeaway: A backup is a copy somewhere else. Systems with one recovered; the one 'too big to back up' did not, and the services that depended on one building stopped together.
verified_claims: The fire was in a server room on the fifth floor of the National Information Resources Service (NIRS) data center in Daejeon; fire authorities received the report at about 8:20 p.m. on Friday 26 September 2025 [Asia News Network; Korea Times].

It started in a lithium-ion UPS battery that had been disconnected for relocation to the basement [Asia News Network]. The exact cause was still under investigation: police believed six of 384 batteries were involved, workers said sparks appeared about 40 minutes after power was cut, and police said accounts were inconsistent [JoongAng Daily, 29 Sept 2025].
The fire was fully extinguished the next day [Korea Times, Asia News Network].
NIRS housed 647 government information systems. 96 were directly damaged by the fire and 551 were shut down as a precaution against heat damage [Asia News Network].
Government websites, Korea Post, Government24 and the mobile ID application were among the disrupted services [Asia News Network].
G-Drive, the government's shared document storage, was destroyed in the fire and was not backed up externally [Korea Times, 2 Oct 2025; JoongAng Daily, 1 Oct 2025].
G-Drive has been in use since 2018, requiring officials to keep work documents in the cloud rather than on personal computers [JoongAng Daily].
G-Drive held about 858 TB [DatacenterDynamics, TechSpot, PC Gamer; not stated in the JoongAng or Korea Times pieces read].

Number of G-Drive users is reported inconsistently: some 191,000 civil servants across 74 agencies [Korea Times, 2 Oct]; files of some 750,000 civil servants, about 30 GB each [Interior Ministry via JoongAng Daily]; about 125,000 actual users, 17% of staff [secondary outlets]. The film shows a range or avoids a count.

The Interior Ministry said most Daejeon systems are backed up daily to separate equipment in the same center and to a remote facility, but G-Drive's large-capacity, low-performance structure did not allow external backup [JoongAng Daily].
Digital government innovation office head Lee Yong-suk called the lack of an external backup 'a mistake' [Korea Times, 2 Oct].

The Ministry of Personnel Management, which required documents be stored only on G-Drive, was hit hardest [JoongAng Daily]. An Interior Ministry director said final reports and official records are also in the OnNara system, so it is 'not a total loss' [JoongAng Daily].

Restoration: 112 of 647 services (17.3%) by noon on 2 Oct [Korea Times]; 631 of 709 administrative services (89%) by 31 Oct, with all 40 Grade 1 essential services back [Korea Times/Yonhap]; 696 of 709 (98.2%) on 14 Nov, 49 days after the fire, with Daejeon complete and 13 of 16 systems relocated to Daegu still being restored [JoongAng Daily]. The denominators differ (647 vs 709) and the film names which one it uses.
The 96 destroyed systems were to be rebuilt at a data center in Daegu [Korea Times, 2 Oct].

Police booked four people (one NIRS employee and three outsourced workers) on suspicion of professional negligence resulting in fire, announced 1 Oct 2025; later reports say five people were charged [JoongAng Daily; DatacenterDynamics headline]. Booking is not a finding of guilt.
anti_patterns: Do not use 'more than 160 services' (the brief's original framing): no source read supports it. Use 647 systems affected, 96 directly burned, 551 shut as a precaution.
Do not mix 647 (systems) and 709 (services) in one sentence as the same quantity.
Do not state a single G-Drive user count as fact; reports range from about 125,000 to 750,000.
Do not say the fire was caused by negligence or name individuals; say police booked people on suspicion and the cause was under investigation.
Do not say 'all government data was lost'. Most systems were restored; G-Drive was lost; final reports also existed in OnNara.
Do not claim G-Drive data was recovered or that 'over 60 percent' of it was, because that figure is unconfirmed.
Do not use a 'breaking news' look, red alert graphics, or footage-style images of the real building.

visual_metaphors.abstract_concept: Hundreds of public services as a wall of labelled folder tabs
visual_metaphors.motion_pattern: scorch front crossing the grid, tabs curl and fall away

visual_metaphors.abstract_concept: A backup as a ghost copy sliding to a remote shelf
visual_metaphors.motion_pattern: ghost copy glides to the far shelf before the burn

scene_blueprint.title: Friday night
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Date, place and the hook: services and records vanishing as a government data center burns
scene_blueprint.visual_action: A wall of folder tabs labelled with public services; an ember in a corner; the scorch front starts to cross the wall

scene_blueprint.title: Batteries on the move
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: What was in the building and how the fire started, with the cause marked as under investigation
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Fifth-floor server room in line art; batteries unplugged and carried toward the basement; sparks; the 8:20 pm report; a question mark over the exact cause

scene_blueprint.title: 647 systems, one building
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Scale of the outage and the split between burned and shut down as a precaution; what citizens lost
scene_blueprint.visual_action: 647 tabs; 96 burn and 551 dim as if switched off; icons for ID app, post office and government portal go grey

scene_blueprint.title: The drive with no copy
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: G-Drive: since 2018, about 858 terabytes, no external backup because of its size; other systems had daily copies
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Ghost copies slide to a remote shelf for ordinary folders; the big central G-Drive folder has nothing underneath it and burns; the 858 TB stamp

scene_blueprint.title: Weeks to come back
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Recovery in stages; some of the ministry's own work lost, but final records also existed elsewhere
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Tally rolls 17% then 89% then 98%; Daegu shelf receives rebuilt folders; one empty folder remains in the middle

scene_blueprint.title: A copy somewhere else
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Accountability is still being sorted out; the lesson is a copy in another place
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Four then five stamped outlines of people marked 'booked / charged: not a finding'; the empty folder holds on a bare desk
